# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 16 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 16

**16:1** And the priest said, "Give back the virgin whom you received from the temple of the Lord." And Joseph burst into tears. The priest said: "I will give you the water of the conviction of the Lord to drink, and it will make your sin manifest before your own eyes."

**16:2** And the priest prepared the water and made Joseph drink of it and sent him into the wilderness. He came back whole. And he made Mary drink and sent her into the wilderness. She came back whole also. And all the people marveled, because sin was not revealed in them.

**16:3** And the priest said: "If the Lord God has not revealed sin in you, neither do I condemn you." And he released them. Joseph took Mary and departed to his house, rejoicing and glorifying the God of Israel.

---

## Translator's Note

The "water of conviction" (*hydōr elegmou Kyriou*) is modeled directly on the ordeal of the "bitter water" administered to a woman suspected of adultery in Numbers 5:11-31. That ritual involved the woman drinking water mixed with dust from the tabernacle floor — if guilty, her body would be afflicted; if innocent, she would be unharmed. By applying this ordeal to both Mary and Joseph, the author accomplishes two things: Joseph is also cleared of any complicity in a cover-up, and the public, witnessed nature of their acquittal replaces any private doubt. The rejoicing in 16:3 mirrors the conclusion of the Joachim-and-Anna crisis (chapters 1-5), creating a narrative rhyme.
